newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus threatens to unmask provocateurs.
newsitem.headline: Belarus threatens to unmask provocateurs.

text.p: Belarus read out a confession on Monday from a Russian television crew held for violating its border and said it would soon reveal who was behind the "provocation".

The detention of the four-man crew from Russia's ORT channel near the border on Friday in a near replay of the arrests of another ORT crew last month, has strained ties between Moscow and Minsk, which signed a union treaty earlier this year.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin has said he might review the treaty aimed at integrating the two countries if Belarus failed to release the ORT journalists.

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, who has consistently accused Russian media of portraying his leadership in a deliberately negative light, accused the journalists of being in the pay of unnamed foreign powers and said he would soon unmask the real culprits.
Interfax-West news agency quoted Lukashenko as saying the journalists had sent him a message naming the people who had sent them to Belarus "under threat of the sack".
He said it would "be clear who stands behind the puppeteers" who planned the correspondents' actions, Interfax said.

Ivan Pashkevich, the deputy head of the presidential administration, told a news conference the ORT correspondent had written the address to Lukashenko from Lida, the town near the Lithuanian border where the crew is being held.
He had also asked for forgiveness, Pashkevich said.

"I carried out an attempt on the state border of Belarus. This action was planned by the ORT leadership. I recognise I carried out a crime. I profoundly regret what happened and ask the president of Belarus not to institute criminal proceedings against us," Pashkevich quoted the correspondent as saying.
The journalists were mere "pawns" in a "dirty political game" he said, adding: "This provocation was directed against us, our state and senior officials in the republic of Belarus."
ORT said Monday's annoucement from Minsk was reminiscent of the tactics of Soviet dictator Josef Stalin.

"This political action by the Belarus authorities is being conducted along the lines of those ominous political shows of the 1930s where innocent people had to play the important role of unmasking themselves," an ORT newsreader said.
"Russian Public Television has always welcomed the Union of Russia and Belarus but we will never put up with it being a union 'at any cost'," ORT said.
"We will never fail to scrupulously record any infringement on international (human) rights in our programmmes."
A spokesman for the Belarus KGB security services told the news conference criminal proceedings had been launched.
A three-man ORT crew was detained on July 26 for illegally crossing the Belarus border. Two of the crew could face five years in prison. The third, a driver, has been released pending trial.

The second crew had intended to show that the Belarussian-Lithuanian border was not clearly defined and that the original arrests of correspondent Pavel Sheremet and his colleagues were politically inspired.
Lukashenko slammed Russia for checking up on his border guards' work.
